name: Platform Governance & Security Practice
description: This practice establishes the automated guardrails, dynamic compliance validation, and integrated observability required to secure the IDP. It focuses heavily on implementing dynamic admission controllers and policy-as-code to enforce enterprise standards securely by default, effectively replacing static, manual compliance checks with proactive, system-enforced governance.

narratives.name: Enterprise Governance and Security
narratives.description: How the IDP replaces manual compliance with proactive automation and immutability.

narrativeContexts.context: A critical value proposition of a mature, enterprise-grade platform is its secure-by-default posture, traditionally enforced by proprietary Security Context Constraints (SCC).

With upstream Kubernetes deprecating basic Pod Security Policies in favor of highly basic admission controllers, relying solely on default RBAC leaves significant governance gaps for enterprise workloads handling sensitive data.

To provide equivalent or superior guardrails, organizations must implement advanced dynamic admission controllers that actively intercept, validate, mutate, and generate Kubernetes resources in real-time.

Furthermore, maintaining this secure posture requires autonomous dependency management systems that continuously scan internal repositories and automatically generate pull requests for critical security flaws across the vast ecosystem of CNCF projects.

alphas.name: Platform Risk And Compliance
alphas.description: Measures the business risk evaluation, security posture validation, and compliance mitigation maturity.

states.name: Identified
states.description: Basic security risks and compliance needs are listed.

checklist.name: Privilege Escalation Risks Mapped
checklist.description: The specific vectors for malicious privilege escalations within multi-tenant clusters are documented and analyzed.

checklist.name: Observability Compliance Defined
checklist.description: Requirements for masking sensitive data in logs and ensuring absolute cross-tenant data isolation are defined.

states.name: Assessed
states.description: Detailed risk assessment matrices and compliance mappings are documented.

checklist.name: Policy Engine Selected
checklist.description: A dynamic admission controller framework (e.g., Kyverno or OPA Gatekeeper) is rigorously selected based on operational efficiency and policy language requirements.

checklist.name: Logging Stack Architected
checklist.description: A multi-tiered approach utilizing Fluentd for lightweight collection and Elasticsearch for rapid search is architected to consolidate ephemeral pod logs securely.

states.name: Mitigated
states.description: Scenario-based behavioral guides mitigate specific user risks.

checklist.name: Privilege Restrictions Active
checklist.description: Policies strictly prevent containers from running as root users and actively block highly privileged containers at admission.

checklist.name: RBAC over Logs Enforced
checklist.description: Strict Role-Based Access Control is implemented over log access, mathematically ensuring developers only access data within their specific namespaces.

states.name: Automated
states.description: Automated compliance auditing and security posture checks are in place.

checklist.name: Automated Mutation Validated
checklist.description: The policy engine autonomously fixes non-compliant configurations by injecting necessary missing annotations or labels into incoming objects.

checklist.name: Resource Generation Active
checklist.description: Default resources, such as granular network policies or role bindings, are automatically generated by the engine whenever a new namespace is provisioned.

checklist.name: Chaos Engineering Conducted
checklist.description: Chaos engineering experiments are continuously executed to validate recovery strategies and empirically verify that automated compliance checks prevent security regressions.

checklist.name: Automated Dependency Scanning
checklist.description: Tools like Renovate autonomously scan complex Kubernetes YAML manifests and Helm charts, reducing Mean Time To Patch (MTTP) for critical vulnerabilities via automated Pull Requests.

alphas.name: Dynamic Policy Enforcement
alphas.description: The specific implementation of policy-as-code engines (like Kyverno or OPA Gatekeeper) applied directly to cluster admission webhooks.

states.name: Defined
states.description: Rules governing application behavior, security standards, and infrastructure state are written in specific policy code formats.

checklist.name: YAML/Rego Policies Codified
checklist.description: Security requirements are translated into Kubernetes-native YAML (for Kyverno) or Rego DSL (for OPA) and committed to version control.

states.name: Applied
states.description: Policies are loaded into the cluster API and are actively rejecting invalid configurations.

checklist.name: Admission Webhooks Registered
checklist.description: The policy engine successfully registers validating webhooks, intercepting API requests prior to persistence in etcd.

states.name: Automated
states.description: Policies intelligently alter requests to conform to enterprise standards without blocking or fracturing developer workflows.

checklist.name: Mutation/Generation Verified
checklist.description: The engine autonomously corrects API payloads based on generation rules, actively reducing developer friction.

workProducts.name: Policy-as-Code Repository
workProducts.description: The central, version-controlled storage of all security constraints, operational guardrails, and compliance rules enforced by the cluster fleet.

levelsOfDetail.name: Descriptive
levelsOfDetail.description: Human-readable lists and matrices of required enterprise constraints (e.g., "no root access").

checklist.name: Governance Requirements Listed
checklist.description: High-level enterprise compliance rules and legal liabilities are documented in plain text matrices.

levelsOfDetail.name: Defined YAML
levelsOfDetail.description: Structured code ready for ingestion and validation by policy engines.

checklist.name: Engine-Specific Syntax Validated
checklist.description: Code cleanly conforms to Kyverno YAML or OPA Rego schema requirements without parsing errors.

levelsOfDetail.name: Automated
levelsOfDetail.description: Comprehensive policy suites integrated directly into the CI/CD pipeline and admission controllers, blocking insecure deployments proactively.

checklist.name: CI/CD Pipeline Integration
checklist.description: Policy validation occurs aggressively in the pipeline before images ever reach live environments.

checklist.name: Full Policy Templates Accessible
checklist.description: Complete policy templates for routine operations are available for automatic generation across new namespaces.

activities.name: Define Security Constraints
activities.description: Translate raw enterprise compliance requirements into specific technical constraints mapping directly to admission controller policies.

activities.name: Implement Admission Controllers
activities.description: Configure, tune, and deploy dynamic admission tools like Kyverno or OPA Gatekeeper to securely intercept and validate all Kubernetes API requests.

activities.name: Automate Compliance Correction
activities.description: Configure policy mutation and generation loops to automatically correct configuration drift, inject required security labels, and instantiate default network policies.

activities.name: Execute Automated Dependency Updates
activities.description: Configure tools like Renovate to continuously parse complex Kubernetes YAML manifests and Helm charts, autonomously generating updates to mitigate CVEs.

personas.name: Security and Controls Lead
personas.description: A specialized role that embeds deep compliance frameworks and highly secure guardrails into platform templates from the very inception of the project.

personas.name: Site Reliability Engineer
personas.description: A specialist who embeds observability, designs aggressive chaos engineering experiments, and implements the automated checks that definitively prevent security regressions.

personaGroups.name: Enterprise Security Team
personaGroups.description: The governance board that defines enterprise compliance mandates and validates architectural security.

personaGroups.name: SRE Guild
personaGroups.description: The operational unit executing reliability patterns, policy implementation, and dependency automation.

patterns.name: Policy Implementation Lifecycle
patterns.description: The structured progression of defining, applying, and completely automating security policies across the IDP fleet.

patternViews.name: Prerequisites
patternViews.description: Initial security requirement gathering and mapping of privilege escalation vectors.

patternViews.name: Policy Definition Phase
patternViews.description: Translating abstract compliance rules into structured code and validating engine syntax.

patternViews.name: Active Enforcement Phase
patternViews.description: Live admission controller interception, automated mutation operations, and continuous dependency scanning.
